tools.name: read_url
tools.description: Read a public http(s) URL as markdown. Uses text/markdown when the server sends it, otherwise Workers AI toMarkdown with images off (no neurons), then a local HTML stripper. Respects robots.txt for BotThruFetcher. Does not cache or store the page.

tools.name: calculate
tools.description: Arithmetic, scientific functions, percentages, and unit conversion. No network and no eval. expression is at most 500 characters. precision is 1 to 34 significant digits, default 15. An unknown symbol returns the supported unit list.

tools.name: extract_page_data
tools.description: Fetch one public HTML page and return title, meta, Open Graph, JSON-LD, links, headings, feeds, and tables. Same SSRF guard and per-network limit as read_url. Cached 10 minutes by final URL. Does not store the page.

tools.name: site_discovery
tools.description: Fetch a site's agent-facing files (robots.txt, llms.txt, sitemap, well-known MCP and agent cards, OpenAPI, security.txt) and say what was found. Does not change the site.

tools.name: check_url
tools.description: Request a public URL and report status, final URL, latency, content type, size, TLS, and a few response headers. Does not follow into private networks.

tools.name: check_mcp_server
tools.description: Connect to a remote streamable-HTTP MCP server: initialize, notifications/initialized, and tools/list. Also lists prompts or resources when advertised. Never calls the remote server's tools.

tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Look up a hostname via Cloudflare DNS (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, CAA, SOA). type email_auth returns MX, SPF, DMARC, and the DNSSEC AD flag. Does not connect to the name.

tools.name: rdap_lookup
tools.description: Registration data for a domain (IANA bootstrap, then the registry RDAP server), or an IP or ASN via rdap.org with RIPEstat as fallback. Returns registrar, dates, status, and nameservers or the network name, country, and holder. No contact emails or street addresses.

tools.name: time_convert
tools.description: Convert a civil time from one IANA time zone to another using Intl. Does not call the network.

tools.name: date_math
tools.description: Add or subtract days, hours, or business days (Monday to Friday, holidays not skipped), or diff two dates. Intl and UTC calendar dates only.

tools.name: holidays
tools.description: Public holidays for a country and year from date.nager.at. Cached for 24 hours. Returns date, name, and local name.

tools.name: exchange_rate
tools.description: Fiat exchange rate from Frankfurter (ECB). No crypto. Cached for 1 hour. amount is converted locally.

tools.name: embed
tools.description: Embed up to 32 strings (8000 characters each) with Workers AI. Default model @cf/baai/bge-m3. Also @cf/google/embeddinggemma-300m. Stops with budget_exhausted before it can use the neurons reserved for /v1/ask.

tools.name: rerank
tools.description: Score up to 32 documents against a query with @cf/baai/bge-reranker-base. Returns indexes and scores, not a rewritten answer. Same daily neuron guard as embed.

tools.name: fetch_page
tools.description: Alias of read_url. Same markdown result, including title, final URL, status, approx_tokens, and any Content-Signal header.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Order window. need is required. status is answered only when a BotThru tool ran, routed when Workers AI wrote a pointer and the task was not done, unsupported when the need was only logged. Do not send secrets or personal data.

tools.name: time
tools.description: Current UTC time, plus the same instant in an IANA time zone. Defaults to UTC.

tools.name: uuid
tools.description: One random UUID (crypto.randomUUID).

tools.name: echo
tools.description: Headers, country, and bot classification of this HTTP request. Cookie and authorization values are redacted.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Which bot BotThru thinks is calling, and why.

findings.detail: Description of "ask" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_url, extract_page_data, check_url, check_mcp_server, fetch_page · Private data: site_discovery, check_url, rdap_lookup, rerank, ask · Public sink: ask, echo · Destructive: calculate.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_url, extract_page_data, check_url, check_mcp_server, fetch_page · Private data: site_discovery, check_url, rdap_lookup, rerank, ask · Public sink: ask, echo · Destructive: calculate

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "ask" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Order window. need is required. status is answered only when time, uuid, echo, or whoami ran; routed is a pointer; unsupported means the need was logged as demand. Do not send secrets or personal data." → after: "Order window. need is required. status is answered only when a BotThru tool ran, routed when Workers AI wrote a pointer and the task was not done, unsupported when the need was only logged. Do not send secrets or personal data."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
